articles.title: Post your questions for Celia Imrie
articles.summary: From Miss Babs in Acorn Antiques to Calendar Girls, The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel and her infamous appearance on The Celebrity Traitors, it’s hard to know where to begin. Celia Imrie has had such a varied career, it’s hard to know where you might know her best from.
body: Maybe you know her as Mrs Quickly, the ghastly would-be stepmother in Nanny McPhee. Or maybe you first encountered her in Upstairs, Downstairs, To the Manor Born, Bergerac, Lovejoy or The Darling Buds of May, or as Claudia Bing, the magnificently awful PR rival of Jennifer Saunders’ Edina in Absolutely Fabulous.

More recently, she returned as Una in Bridget Jones: Mad About the Boy; joined Helen Mirren, Pierce Brosnan and Ben Kingsley in The Thursday Murder Club; and popped up in The Diplomat. Then, of course, there was The Celebrity Traitors. Imrie entered the castle as a Faithful, survived being chained up in a wooden cabin, and accidentally farted while doing so – instantly producing the Guardian’s No 2 TV moment of the year – and eventually got murdered in plain sight by Alan Carr.

Now she’s back as in (yes, it’s nearly that time already) Merry Christmas Aubrey Flint, alongside John Bradley as a Christmas-hating model-soldier painter sentenced to community service at a struggling retirement home, where he somehow ends up directing a chaotic production of A Christmas Carol. Richard E Grant and Jim Broadbent are along for the festive ride, too.

articles.title: Disney+ to Name New Australia Commissioner, Keeps Southeast Asia ‘On the Menu’ as It Triples Local Output
articles.summary: Disney+ is about to name a new commissioner in Australia and has not ruled out a return to production in Southeast Asia, Jon Wax, executive VP of international original television at Disney Entertainment, said Wednesday at the Busan International Film Festival.
body: Asked whether production would resume in markets such as Indonesia after earlier cutbacks, Wax said Disney+ is exploring specific titles there. “It is absolutely on the menu. We just need some time to execute,” he said.

Local versions of Korean unscripted hit “ Battle of Fates,” confirmed in development in March, are now in prep, Wax said. In the supernatural competition series, practitioners of shamanism, tarot, face reading and saju go up against each other. It became the biggest series premiere ever on Disney+ in Korea and has since led to a spinoff, “House of Fates.” Wax said the U.S. team moved quickly when Choi Yeon-woo, who runs the Disney+ content operation in Korea, and her team first brought the show to them.

Wax said the show felt culturally distinct, given the privileged position its subject holds in Korean society, “but every society on Earth has their practitioners of this. And we felt like if this works, this could be something that could be shot in other countries.”

articles.title: ‘Vikings’ Actor Gustaf Skarsgard Makes Feature Directorial Debut With Psychological Horror ‘The Cannibal’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Swedish actor Gustaf Skarsgård, best known for “Vikings,” has started production on his feature directorial debut, psychological horror film “The Cannibal.” The film, written by Peter Birro, is a nightmarish journey into a screenwriter’s mind as he returns to Ingmar Bergman’s home island of Fårö in…
body: Swedish actor Gustaf Skarsgård, best known for “Vikings,” has started production on his feature directorial debut, psychological horror film “The Cannibal.”

Skarsgård said, “There is no way to approach Bergman but from deep within the gigantic cinematic shadow the titan casts. Just like the main character David tries to break free from his demonic magnetism, so too the movie itself will attempt to break free in a playful way, by using his own artistic tools.”

Birro said, “When I was a young screenwriter, I got to meet Ingmar Bergman on his desolate island of Fårö. He told me about his demons and showed me where he kept them: locked away in the freezer. For 30 years, I’ve been longing to open that freezer door and let the demons out. Now the time has come.”
Producer Martin Persson said, “ ‘The Cannibal’ is a very exciting, fun and surprising film dealing with how much one would be prepared to sacrifice to make great art.”

articles.title: ‘Will You Still Be My Friend’ Director Lu Po-Shun on Finding Common Ground From San Sebastian to Busan
articles.summary: When Variety spoke with Taiwanese director Lu Po-Shun in March, he was seeking final financing for his debut feature, “Will You Still Be My Friend,” a coming-of-age drama weaving adolescent friendship with local politics and solar energy development.
body: Developing the short into a feature drew on Lu’s extensive field research in the area where he grew up, allowing him to develop a fuller portrait of local politics. The film has since earned Golden Horse nominations for adapted screenplay and new performer for Jaden Wang. “I built the feature out of the short by mapping out each character’s arc, giving everyone a clear beginning, development, turning point and resolution,” Lu said. “The key events then drove the story forward, bringing it together into a complete narrative.”
The challenge, however, was deciding how much of the adults’ world to retain.

“The adult storylines were actually more complicated and more explicit in the full script,” Lu said. “But in the edit, with limited running time, explaining those events too clearly would have sent the narrative in too many directions and risked taking the audience’s attention away from the two boys. So we chose to make those storylines less explicit, allowing them to emerge more through the changes in the children’s relationship.”

articles.title: Noel Gallagher and Susan Sarandon among celebrities to sign Drumcree march letter
articles.summary: The letter, addressed to NI Secretary Sir Chris Bryant, calls on an international mediator to be appointed to find a resolution to the parade dispute.
body: Oasis' Noel Gallagher, Oscar winner Susan Sarandon and Line of Duty star Adrian Dunbar are among dozens to sign a letter in support of residents in a stand-off over a decision to allow a parade down a predominantly nationalist road.
There has been 11 days of deadlock between Garvaghy Road residents and the local Orange Order over the proposed march in Portadown, County Armagh.
While peaceful, the stalemate has reopened what was once the most bitter parading dispute in Northern Ireland.
Other people to have signed the letter include musician Paul Weller, Derry Girls star Siobhán McSweeney and The Smiths' Johnny Marr.

articles.title: What can I do to protect myself after 'Asos hacked' message?
articles.summary: Asos says people should not engage with the unauthorised notification and says it'll provide further information.
body: If a strange-looking message from Asos popped up on your phone on Tuesday, you may be worrying what it could mean and whether you need to do anything.
The online retailer has emailed customers apologising for the "unauthorised push notification" containing an external link, adding that they should disregard the message and not click on it.
Here's what has happened, and what those who may have been affected are being advised to do.
On Tuesday morning, Asos users across the UK were sent pop-up messages from its app that appear to have been sent by hackers trying to extort the company.

articles.title: 24 Hour Party People review – daring metatextual paean to the Manchester music scene
articles.summary: Rereleased for its 24th anniversary, Michael Winterbottom’s freewheeling film about a journalist who championed post-punk bands couldn’t have starred anyone but Steve Coogan. Michael Winterbottom’s intriguing, daring, freewheeling movie is being rereleased for its 24th anniversary.
body: From there, he develops a remarkable and even unique identity as the post-punk patron. He insists on freedom of expression for all the bands he mentors and promotes, with no real contract other than a bizarre document signed in his blood – to the later astonishment of London music executive Roger Ames, played by Keith Allen, who realises that Wilson does not have legal rights to the back catalogue that Factory Records has amassed.

Peter Kay plays the lairy club owner that Wilson first does business with; Lennie James is Factory co-founder Alan Erasmus; Andy Serkis is producer Martin Hannett; Shirley Henderson is Wilson’s first wife, Lindsay, who has a fictionalised fling with Magazine lead singer Howard Devoto, which the real Devoto comes on to dispute. Sean Harris gives a stark and spiky performance as the legendary Ian Curtis, the Joy Division lead singer who was to take his own life (a very different performance from Sam Riley’s more empathetic portrayal in Anton Corbijn’s film Control ).

articles.title: Eva Marie Saint: the Hitchcock Blonde who outgrew the persona
articles.summary: Her glacial poise in North By Northwest made her a cinematic icon, but films including On the Waterfront and Loving revealed great subtlety alongside the glamour. Eva Marie Saint dies aged 102. Her best films – ranked. Her life in pictures. ‘I’m Eve Kendall. I’m 26 and unmarried.
body: Not quite everything. That is the famously succinct introduction given in a swaying dining car in a voice creamy with insinuation. Eve is speaking to Cary Grant’s fugitive ad man Roger Thornhill, wrongly accused of murder and hiding out from the cops on a train from New York to Chicago in Alfred Hitchcock’s 1959 classic North By Northwest. Eve is going to hide him in her compartment because she wants to have sex with him, and much later that train of theirs is to symbolically enter a tunnel. But is that the whole story? Eve’s amazingly beautiful, enigmatic face encodes a secret.

She is of course played by Eva Marie Saint, a star whose three names each hinted in their ways at purity and piety; they gave this stylish, assured performer a hint of something respectable, even prim that the passion could work against.
